en.greeting: Hi! Today we go back in time a little: was and were, the past of am, is and are. Let's take it step by step.

steps.title: was and were
steps.text: You know am, is and are for now. For the past, English uses just two words.
steps.body: Remember: Indonesian says *Saya di rumah* with no extra word, but English needs **am / is / are** (*I am at home*). For the past, **am** and **is** become **was**; **are** becomes **were**. So **I was**, **he/she/it was**, but **you were**, **we were**, **they were**. Why *you were*, even for one person? Because *you* always goes with *are* (you are), and *are* becomes *were*. Indonesian only adds a time word (*Kemarin saya sakit*), but English changes the word too: **Yesterday I was sick**, not 'Yesterday I am sick'.

steps.title: Past time words
steps.text: These time words tell you: use was or were.

timeline.title: Before now and now
timeline.caption: Before now (last year, last week, yesterday, last night) → was / were. Now → am / is / are.

steps.title: In real sentences
steps.text: Here are was and were in everyday sentences. First look at who or what the sentence is about (the **subject**: *I, my mother, the nasi goreng*), then choose was or were.
steps.body: **you** always takes **were**, even for one person (because it's *you are* now). Two names, like Rina and Budi, = **they** → **were**. One thing, like *the nasi goreng*, = **it** → **was**.

examples.en: I was at the office yesterday.
My mother was in Surabaya last week.
examples.id: Ibu saya di Surabaya minggu lalu.

examples.en: The nasi goreng was delicious.
We were tired last night.
You were late this morning.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Two friends, one weekend. Which verb fits?

question.prompt: Complete: Rina and Dewi ___ at the market last Saturday.
question.explanation: **Rina and Dewi** are two people = **they**, so the verb is **were**. **last Saturday** is the past, so not **are**, and **was** is only for one person or thing.

steps.title: Saying no: wasn't and weren't
steps.text: Negatives are easy: just add **not** after was or were.
steps.body: **was not → wasn't**, **were not → weren't** (the **'** shows the missing *o*). Don't add any other word, and don't put not first: 'She not was busy' is wrong. *The rooms* = **they** → **weren't**. In English, **they** is also for things (rooms, shoes, tickets), not only for people like *mereka*.

examples.en: I wasn't at work yesterday.
The bus wasn't full this morning.
Rina and Budi weren't at school on Monday.
examples.id: Rina dan Budi tidak masuk sekolah hari Senin.

examples.en: The rooms weren't clean.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Budi tells you about a concert last Saturday.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Tiket konsernya tidak mahal.
question.explanation: **The concert tickets** are more than one (tickets has -s) = **they**. In English *they* is for things too, not only for people. So the negative is **weren't** (were not), right after the subject: **The concert tickets weren't expensive.**

steps.title: Asking questions
steps.text: To ask a yes/no question, move was or were to the front.
steps.body: Put **Was/Were before the subject** (who or what you ask about): He was at home → **Was he at home?** In Indonesian you can ask by just raising your voice (*Dia di rumah?*), but in English don't just add a question mark to a normal sentence: move was/were to the front. Answer with a short answer that repeats was/were: **Yes, he was.** / **No, it wasn't.** (Indonesian says *Ya* or *Ya, bagus*; English needs the was/were.) If someone asks **Were you…?**, they ask about you, so answer with **I**.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: You want to ask a colleague about Sari.

options: Sari was at the office yesterday?
Were Sari at the office yesterday?
Was Sari at the office yesterday?
question.prompt: Which question means 'Apakah Sari di kantor kemarin?'
question.explanation: In a question, **was/were** comes before the subject (here *Sari*). **Sari** = she → **was**: **Was Sari at the office yesterday?** The first option is statement order with a question mark, and **were** doesn't go with one person (except you).

steps.title: Listen and answer
steps.text: Your friend Budi asks you a question. Press play and listen.

question.listen: Were you at the cinema last night?
question.prompt: Listen to Budi's question. The answer is yes. Choose your short answer.
question.explanation: Budi asks **Were you at the cinema last night?** It's a question about you, so answer with **I** + **was**: **Yes, I was.** 'Yes, you were' talks about Budi, and 'he' is someone else.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip through these cards to lock in was and were.

flashcards.back: was (I was, she was, it was)
were (you were, we were, they were)

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Keep it for later.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · was / were
artifact.intro: The past of am, is and are: positive sentences, negatives and questions.
tips: A past time word (yesterday, last night, last week) means **was/were**, not am/is/are.
**you** always takes **were**: **You were late**, not 'You was late'.
Questions start with **Was/Were**: **Were they busy?** Short answers repeat it: **Yes, they were.** / **No, it wasn't.**
**they** is for things too: **The rooms were clean.** / **My shoes weren't cheap.**

examples.en: How was your weekend? — It was great!
My phone wasn't cheap.
Was the film good? — Yes, it was.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita sedikit kembali ke masa lalu: was dan were, bentuk lampau dari am, is dan are. Ayo kita pelajari pelan-pelan.

steps.title: was dan were
steps.text: Kamu sudah tahu am, is dan are untuk sekarang. Untuk masa lalu, bahasa Inggris hanya memakai dua kata.
steps.body: Ingat: bahasa Indonesia bilang *Saya di rumah* tanpa kata tambahan, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh **am / is / are** (*I am at home*). Untuk masa lalu, **am** dan **is** menjadi **was**; **are** menjadi **were**. Jadi **I was**, **he/she/it was**, tapi **you were**, **we were**, **they were**. Kenapa *you were*, walaupun hanya satu orang? Karena *you* selalu berpasangan dengan *are* (you are), dan *are* menjadi *were*. Bahasa Indonesia cukup menambah kata waktu (*Kemarin saya sakit*), tapi bahasa Inggris juga mengubah katanya: **Yesterday I was sick**, bukan 'Yesterday I am sick'.

steps.title: Kata waktu lampau
steps.text: Kata-kata waktu ini memberi tanda: pakai was atau were.

timeline.title: Sebelum sekarang dan sekarang
timeline.caption: Sebelum sekarang (last year, last week, yesterday, last night) → was / were. Sekarang → am / is / are.

steps.title: Dalam kalimat nyata
steps.text: Ini contoh was dan were dalam kalimat sehari-hari. Lihat dulu siapa atau apa yang dibicarakan (**subjek**: *I, my mother, the nasi goreng*), lalu pilih was atau were.
steps.body: **you** selalu memakai **were**, walaupun hanya satu orang (karena sekarang pun *you are*). Dua nama, seperti Rina dan Budi, = **they** → **were**. Satu benda, seperti *the nasi goreng*, = **it** → **was**.

examples.en: I was at the office yesterday.
My mother was in Surabaya last week.
examples.id: Ibu saya di Surabaya minggu lalu.

examples.en: The nasi goreng was delicious.
We were tired last night.
You were late this morning.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Dua teman, satu akhir pekan. Kata kerja mana yang cocok?

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Rina and Dewi ___ at the market last Saturday.
question.explanation: **Rina and Dewi** itu dua orang = **they**, jadi kata kerjanya **were**. **last Saturday** itu masa lalu, jadi bukan **are**, dan **was** hanya untuk satu orang atau benda.

steps.title: Kalimat negatif: wasn't dan weren't
steps.text: Kalimat negatif itu mudah: cukup tambahkan **not** setelah was atau were.
steps.body: **was not → wasn't**, **were not → weren't** (tanda **'** menggantikan huruf *o* yang hilang). Jangan tambah kata lain, dan jangan taruh not di depan: 'She not was busy' itu salah. *The rooms* = **they** → **weren't**. Dalam bahasa Inggris, **they** juga dipakai untuk benda (kamar, sepatu, tiket), bukan hanya untuk orang seperti *mereka*.

examples.en: I wasn't at work yesterday.
The bus wasn't full this morning.
Rina and Budi weren't at school on Monday.
examples.id: Rina dan Budi tidak masuk sekolah hari Senin.

examples.en: The rooms weren't clean.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Budi bercerita tentang konser hari Sabtu lalu.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Tiket konsernya tidak mahal.
question.explanation: **The concert tickets** lebih dari satu (tickets ada -s), jadi = **they**. Dalam bahasa Inggris *they* juga dipakai untuk benda, bukan hanya orang. Jadi bentuk negatifnya **weren't** (were not), langsung setelah subjek: **The concert tickets weren't expensive.**

steps.title: Membuat pertanyaan
steps.text: Untuk pertanyaan ya/tidak, pindahkan was atau were ke depan.
steps.body: Taruh **Was/Were di depan subjek** (siapa atau apa yang kamu tanyakan): He was at home → **Was he at home?** Dalam bahasa Indonesia kamu bisa bertanya hanya dengan menaikkan nada suara (*Dia di rumah?*), tapi dalam bahasa Inggris jangan hanya menambah tanda tanya di akhir kalimat biasa: pindahkan was/were ke depan. Jawab dengan jawaban singkat yang mengulang was/were: **Yes, he was.** / **No, it wasn't.** (Bahasa Indonesia cukup *Ya* atau *Ya, bagus*; bahasa Inggris perlu was/were.) Kalau ada yang bertanya **Were you…?**, dia bertanya tentang kamu, jadi jawab dengan **I**.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Kamu mau bertanya kepada rekan kerja tentang Sari.

options: Sari was at the office yesterday?
Were Sari at the office yesterday?
Was Sari at the office yesterday?
question.prompt: Pertanyaan mana yang artinya 'Apakah Sari di kantor kemarin?'
question.explanation: Dalam pertanyaan, **was/were** ada di depan subjek (di sini *Sari*). **Sari** = she → **was**: **Was Sari at the office yesterday?** Pilihan pertama masih susunan kalimat biasa yang diberi tanda tanya, dan **were** tidak dipakai untuk satu orang (kecuali you).

steps.title: Dengar dan jawab
steps.text: Temanmu Budi bertanya sesuatu. Tekan play dan dengarkan.

question.listen: Were you at the cinema last night?
question.prompt: Dengarkan pertanyaan Budi. Jawabannya ya. Pilih jawaban singkatmu.
question.explanation: Budi bertanya **Were you at the cinema last night?** Itu pertanyaan tentang kamu, jadi jawab dengan **I** + **was**: **Yes, I was.** 'Yes, you were' berarti tentang Budi, dan 'he' orang lain.

steps.title: Ulasan cepat
steps.text: Balik kartu-kartu ini supaya was dan were makin melekat.

artifact.title: Ringkasan · was / were
artifact.intro: Bentuk lampau dari am, is dan are: kalimat positif, negatif dan pertanyaan.
tips: Ada kata waktu lampau (yesterday, last night, last week) berarti pakai **was/were**, bukan am/is/are.
**you** selalu memakai **were**: **You were late**, bukan 'You was late'.
Pertanyaan diawali **Was/Were**: **Were they busy?** Jawaban singkat mengulangnya: **Yes, they were.** / **No, it wasn't.**
**they** juga untuk benda: **The rooms were clean.** / **My shoes weren't cheap.**

examples.en: How was your weekend? — It was great!
My phone wasn't cheap.
Was the film good? — Yes, it was.
